claims.statement: Talon is experimental, and scheduled cron invocations are unattended: the host invokes them without approval or authorization handlers, while the runtime auto-rejects approval interrupts for requests marked `trigger: "cron"`.

The agent-facing scheduler supports only relative one-shot and recurring intervals, one-shot and daily timezone-explicit wall-clock schedules, and timezone-explicit five-field cron or listed macros; schedule text is bounded to 200 characters.

Cron implements five fields with ranges, steps, lists, month and weekday aliases, limited L/W/# calendar extensions, and Vixie day-of-month/day-of-week behavior: OR only when neither textual day field starts with `*`, otherwise AND.
Parsed cron expressions and resolved schedule zones use bounded 128-entry caches because expressions and zone names come from agent-supplied input.

Wall-clock, `until`, and cron schedules evaluate local candidates in an explicit IANA zone: nonexistent local times advance to the first valid minute, ambiguous fall-back times use the earlier occurrence, and skipped cron candidates coalesce to one fire.

Cron jobs persist a self-contained prompt, assistant, origin, parsed schedule, repeat/enabled state, timestamps, outcome/error, `until`, and claim timestamp in a versioned JSON store; writes use restrictive directory/file modes and fsynced atomic replacement, while unreadable or wrong-version stores are logged and treated as empty.

Create/list/edit/remove tools are scoped to the current provider and channel-level origin scope: Slack C/G threads share their parent channel and Discord threads use `history_chat` when available; message ID is stored but does not participate in that comparison.

A recurring job's repeat count is consumed at claim time; interval schedules preserve their phase across late ticks and skip to a future interval after downtime, while one-shots and exhausted repeats disable before the run.
`until` is valid only for recurring jobs and is inclusive, with a five-minute late-claim grace; occurrences missed past that grace are disabled and dropped rather than delivered late.

Each scheduler tick first sweeps finished records, then claims due jobs by persisting their advanced next-run state before invocation; after a result it records success or error, suppresses empty or `[SILENT]` output, and changes the outcome to error if delivery fails.

Finished or expired jobs without an error or unresolved claim are removed on a later sweep; failed final runs and interrupted claims are retained for inspection until explicit retention pruning removes disabled completed records.

The scheduler processes due jobs sequentially but survives an unexpected tick failure; the host runs each job on a locked dedicated cron thread with a timeout and interruption recovery, and sends non-silent output to the recorded origin channel.

A cron execution carries durable origin metadata for tool scope and may read the resolved origin history, but it runs on a dedicated cron thread with archive scope disabled, so the scheduled prompt and execution do not create an attended turn or transcript archive entry.

When an operator revokes a paired sender through the running host, Talon cancels that sender's active conversation work, pauses enabled jobs whose stored provider and creator sender ID match, and cancels in-flight scheduled runs; a revoked cron run becomes an error and is not delivered.

The `deepagents-talon pairing pause-jobs <channel> <sender_id>` CLI is documented as a stopped-host operation because the running host is the cron store's only writer; it pauses enabled jobs created by that sender on the channel.
The standard Talon host wiring attaches a `PersistentCronScheduler` only when at least one channel is configured, connecting the cron store to host run and delivery callbacks.

All live CronJobStore instances targeting the same resolved `jobs.json` path share a reentrant lock that serializes complete storage reads and mutations within one process, but it does not coordinate other processes, external writers, execution, or delivery.

CronJobStore caches parsed records by the source file's modification-time, size, and inode identity; it captures that identity with `fstat` on the open handle so an atomic replacement cannot associate older bytes with a newer pathname identity.

Scheduled delivery resolves the recorded provider's channel adapter and selects the parent channel or thread from `deliver_to`; successful non-silent delivery may be recorded in conversation delivery history.
The agent-facing schedule help lists five cron macros, while the parser additionally accepts `@annually` and `@midnight` as aliases.

Concurrency tests exercise all mutations and exclusive claiming through two separate CronJobStore instances sharing a path, verifying that a concurrent creation survives and only one claimant consumes a repeat occurrence.
Schedule timezone resolution accepts only `UTC` or IANA region names and rejects bare UTC offsets and legacy POSIX aliases so recurring schedules retain future daylight-saving rules.

The standard delivery callback logs and drops output when no configured channel serves a job's recorded origin instead of raising, leaving the scheduler's previously recorded successful run status unchanged.
